subject: Mid-contract uplift: accelerated top-up & proportional rebilling
messages:
From: Sarah Winters <sarah.winters@meditech.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@meditech.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

Hi Kim —

We need to add committed capacity this quarter to cover an unexpected product launch. Legal/procurement asked whether Redwood can: (1) apply an accelerated uplift (one-time committed top-up) to our existing yearly commitment; and (2) bill that uplift proportionally to our existing co-term so we don't end up with misaligned invoices across Q4.

Key ask: can you provide a compact proposal with pricing, an invoice timing option (one-time vs monthly amortization), and wording for a short amendment? Procurement would like to avoid creating a separate annual contract that runs off-cycle.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
SVP Product, Meditech Health

---
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Winters <sarah.winters@meditech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the note — we can absolutely support an accelerated top-up and align billing to your co-term. I pulled the account and sketched two practical options so procurement can choose the least disruptive path: one-time invoice for the uplift (faster recognition) or amortized monthly rebilling until co-term.

Im looping in Neha and Ben to confirm price bands and Monica to make sure finance is OK with the proposed invoice mechanics. Well send a short amendment draft and a term-sheet.csv you can circulate with procurement.

Propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow if youd like to go through both options live.

Cheers,
Kim Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

Team —

I pulled usage trends and their committed profile. Quick notes:
- Current annual commit: 3.2M tokens/day equivalent (co-term 2027-02-15).
- Customer asks for +45% capacity effective immediately (~1.44M tokens/day).
- They prefer not to create a separate annual contract.

Pricing thoughts:
1) Accelerated one-time uplift: apply a 10% uplift charge off list for one-time committed top-up (discounted since theyre already committed customers). Finance gets immediate invoice.
2) Proportional rebilling to co-term: convert the top-up into a time-phased commitment that amortizes from effective date to co-term date (pro rata monthly). Slightly higher price (~12% uplift vs list) because it stretches billing.

If we want to be competitive, consider a middle ground: 11% uplift + option to convert remaining to full-year commit at renewal (credit applied).

Ben — need your read on customer willingness and whether Sales will accept the 11% anchor. Monica — any constraints from accounting on creating amortized sub-commitments that roll into the original co-term?

-Neha

---
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

Sounds reasonable. Customer has been high-touch; Id recommend the 11% midpoint with a small signing credit (1% of uplift) if they sign amendment within 7 days. Keeps economics predictable and gives them a quick yes.

Monica — confirm we can invoice: (A) one-time lump sum; or (B) monthly amortized invoices with memo linking to original contract. If amortized, we also need the month-by-month schedule in our billing system.

-Ben

---
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 14:51:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

All — finance can support both flows. Notes: 
- One-time invoice: simplest. We will generate an invoice referencing amendment RW-9827-AM01 and recognize revenue per ASC 606 over remaining period.
- Amortized monthly invoices: we can create a subline item and bill month-to-month, with a reconciliation entry at co-term. We need the exact effective date and token/day quantity by 3PM PT to seed the schedule.
- For audit trail: include the amendment number on each invoice and attach the signed amendment PDF.

Ill prepare the invoice schedule template and attach it to the amendment draft.

-Monica

---
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Winters <sarah.winters@meditech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, procurement@meditech.com
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick context. Attached is a short amendment draft and a two-option term sheet (see redwood-uplift-term-sheet.xlsx). Summary of the two options: 

Option A — Lump-sum accelerated uplift
- One-time invoice for full uplift amount (effective immediately).
- Pricing: 11% uplift off list for the incremental capacity.
- Immediate provisioning; invoice due 30 days.
- Amendment: RW-9827-AM01 (attached PDF stub).

Option B — Proportional rebill to co-term
- Convert uplift into a time-phased commitment billed monthly from effective date to co-term (2027-02-15).
- Pricing: 12% uplift off list (amortization premium).
- Monthly invoices with amortization schedule; final reconciliation at co-term.

We also propose a 1% signing credit on the uplift if the amendment is executed within 7 business days. Finance has confirmed both billing mechanics are supported.

Next steps: pick Option A or B (or tell us preference on hybrid); confirm effective date (we proposed 2026-09-25); and indicate recipient for the DocuSign. Ive included a DocuSign powerform link if procurement wants to e-sign without redlines.

Attachments: Meditech_MA-ChangeRequest.pdf (amendment stub), redwood-uplift-term-sheet.xlsx (two-option pricing + invoice schedule).

If youd like to review on a call, Neha and I are free tomorrow 10:00-10:30 PT.

Best,
Kim Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
From: Sarah Winters <sarah.winters@meditech.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@meditech.com, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract capacity top-up & billing approach

Thanks Kim — procurement reviewed the two options. They prefer Option B (proportional rebill) to avoid a large one-time charge hitting this quarters books. Please proceed with the amendment and the amortization schedule using an effective date of 2026-09-25.

Can you send the DocuSign link to procurement@meditech.com and add the contact: Aaron Blake (aaron.blake@meditech.com) as the signer? Once we have the signed amendment well push the PO through.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah
SVP Product, Meditech Health
